$comment: Learning tracks for /learn. Lessons are written in order by scripts/guide.mjs (2 per week in CI, or `npm run guide`). 'covers' briefs the writer; 'tags' link lessons to related digest posts. Add lessons or tracks freely; unwritten ones show as 'coming soon'.

tracks.title: LLM Foundations
tracks.description: What actually happens inside a large language model, from tokens to training to serving, explained for engineers.

lessons.title: How LLMs work: tokens, embeddings and the transformer
lessons.summary: Follow one prompt through a model: tokenization, embeddings, attention layers and next-token prediction.
lessons.covers: Tokenization (BPE) and why token counts matter; embeddings as vectors; self-attention intuitively (query/key/value) and multi-head attention; the decoder-only transformer stack; next-token prediction and the autoregressive loop; logits, softmax, temperature. Use one running example prompt.

lessons.title: Training an LLM: pretraining, fine-tuning and preference tuning
lessons.summary: How a model goes from random weights to a helpful assistant, and what each training stage contributes.
lessons.covers: Pretraining objective and data scale; loss and gradient descent at a high level; supervised fine-tuning (instruction tuning); preference tuning (RLHF, DPO) and what it changes; LoRA and parameter-efficient fine-tuning; when you as an engineer should fine-tune versus prompt or use RAG.

lessons.title: Inference and serving: sampling, KV cache and batching
lessons.summary: Why generation is memory-bound, how the KV cache works, and the tricks serving systems use to go fast.
lessons.covers: Prefill vs decode phases; why decode is memory-bandwidth bound; the KV cache and its memory cost (with a worked size calculation); sampling strategies; continuous batching and PagedAttention; quantization; speculative decoding; latency metrics (TTFT, tokens/sec) and cost per token.

lessons.title: Context windows and long context: what fits and what works
lessons.summary: What the context window really is, why long context is expensive, and where models lose track.
lessons.covers: Context window as working memory; quadratic attention cost and efficient attention; position encodings (RoPE) and length extrapolation; 'lost in the middle' and needle-in-a-haystack tests; prompt caching and why prefix stability matters; long context vs RAG trade-offs.

lessons.title: Reasoning models and test-time compute
lessons.summary: How models that 'think before answering' work, and when extra thinking is worth the cost.
lessons.covers: Chain-of-thought prompting vs trained reasoning; test-time compute scaling; how reasoning models are trained (RL on verifiable rewards) at a high level; effort/thinking budgets; cost and latency trade-offs; tasks that benefit and tasks that don't.

tracks.title: RAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
tracks.description: Give models your own data: what RAG is, how each stage works, and how to make it accurate in production.

lessons.title: What RAG is, and when to use it
lessons.summary: The retrieve-then-generate pattern, the problems it solves, and how it compares with fine-tuning and long context.
lessons.covers: Why models hallucinate and lack private/fresh knowledge; the RAG pipeline end to end (ingest, index, retrieve, augment, generate) with a diagram; a minimal example; RAG vs fine-tuning vs long context decision table; citations and grounding.

lessons.title: Chunking and embeddings: preparing your data
lessons.summary: How documents become searchable vectors, and why chunking decisions make or break retrieval.
lessons.covers: What embedding models do; cosine similarity; chunk size and overlap trade-offs; structure-aware chunking (headings, tables, code); metadata; contextual chunk enrichment; re-embedding costs when models change; document parsing pitfalls (PDFs, tables).

lessons.title: Vector search and retrieval: ANN indexes, hybrid search and reranking
lessons.summary: How vector databases find similar chunks fast, and how hybrid search and rerankers improve what you retrieve.
lessons.covers: Exact vs approximate nearest neighbour; HNSW and IVF intuitively with recall/latency/memory trade-offs; vector database vs vector index in an existing DB; BM25 keyword search; hybrid search and reciprocal rank fusion; cross-encoder rerankers; filtering by metadata; storage and memory footprint of indexes.

lessons.title: Evaluating and debugging RAG
lessons.summary: How to measure whether your RAG system retrieves the right things and answers faithfully.
lessons.covers: Separating retrieval quality from generation quality; retrieval metrics (recall@k, MRR); faithfulness and answer relevance; building a golden question set; LLM-as-judge and its biases; common failure modes and a debugging checklist; monitoring in production.

lessons.title: Advanced RAG: query rewriting, GraphRAG and agentic retrieval
lessons.summary: Techniques for the hard cases: vague questions, multi-hop reasoning and very large corpora.
lessons.covers: Query rewriting and decomposition; HyDE; multi-hop retrieval; GraphRAG and knowledge graphs (what problem they solve, costs); agentic retrieval where the model decides what to search; caching; when advanced techniques are not worth it.

tracks.title: Agents & Harness Engineering
tracks.description: Build systems where models use tools and act over many steps, and engineer the harness that makes them reliable.

lessons.title: What an AI agent is: the tool-use loop
lessons.summary: From a single model call to a loop that plans, calls tools and observes results.
lessons.covers: Function/tool calling mechanics (schema in, structured call out, result back); the agent loop with a sequence diagram; workflows vs agents and when to use which; a minimal agent in pseudocode; stopping conditions; cost and latency growth with steps.

lessons.title: Harness engineering: everything around the model
lessons.summary: The harness is the code, prompts, tools and guardrails that turn a model into a dependable system, and it often matters more than the model.
lessons.covers: Define the harness (system prompt, tool set, context assembly, loop control, memory, permissions, retries, observability); examples of harnesses such as coding agents; why the same model performs very differently in different harnesses; design principles: small sharp tools, clear tool descriptions, explicit verification steps, human-in-the-loop checkpoints; failure modes the harness must handle.

lessons.title: Context engineering: deciding what the model sees
lessons.summary: Managing the context window across long tasks: what to include, summarize, cache or leave out.
lessons.covers: Context as a scarce budget; structuring system prompt vs task vs retrieved data; just-in-time retrieval vs preloading; compaction and summarization of history; memory files and scratchpads; sub-agents to isolate context; prompt caching and prefix stability; context poisoning and distraction.

lessons.title: Designing tools and the Model Context Protocol (MCP)
lessons.summary: How to design tools models use well, and how MCP standardizes connecting models to tools and data.
lessons.covers: Tool design: names, descriptions, parameter schemas, error messages the model can act on, idempotency; granularity trade-offs; MCP architecture (hosts, clients, servers; tools, resources, prompts) with a diagram; security: least privilege, prompt injection through tool results, approval gates.

lessons.title: Evaluating agents and making them reliable
lessons.summary: How to test systems that take many non-deterministic steps, and the patterns that make them production-ready.
lessons.covers: Why agent evals differ from model evals; task-based evals with graders (code checks, LLM judges, human review); trajectory vs outcome evaluation; pass@k and variance; regression suites; observability and tracing; guardrails, budgets, timeouts and fallbacks; incremental rollout.

tracks.title: AI Infrastructure & Data
tracks.description: The systems underneath AI, with a focus on storage and data movement: training clusters, checkpoints, datasets and serving.

lessons.title: AI training infrastructure: GPUs, networking and parallelism
lessons.summary: What a training cluster looks like and how work is split across thousands of GPUs.
lessons.covers: GPU memory and compute basics; data, tensor, pipeline parallelism and sharded optimizers (ZeRO/FSDP) intuitively; interconnects (NVLink, InfiniBand/RoCE) and why the network matters; failure rates at scale and why checkpointing is essential.

lessons.title: Storage for AI: datasets, checkpoints and data pipelines
lessons.summary: The storage patterns AI workloads create, from feeding GPUs to writing multi-terabyte checkpoints.
lessons.covers: I/O patterns of training (random small reads of datasets vs large sequential checkpoint writes); parallel file systems vs object storage vs tiered caches; checkpoint size math and write bandwidth needs; async and incremental checkpointing; data loaders and GPU starvation; dataset versioning; how vendors (parallel FS, object stores) position for AI.

lessons.title: Data mobility for AI: moving, replicating and protecting AI data
lessons.summary: Migration, replication and backup applied to AI: datasets, checkpoints, vector indexes and model artifacts.
lessons.covers: Moving datasets to where GPUs are (cloud bursting, multi-region); replicating checkpoints for resilience and RPO/RTO for training jobs; backing up vector databases and embeddings (and when re-embedding is cheaper); model artifact registries and provenance; data gravity and egress costs; consistency concerns when copying live indexes.

lessons.title: Serving models at scale: from one GPU to a fleet
lessons.summary: How production systems route, batch, cache and autoscale model inference.
lessons.covers: Model servers and continuous batching; prefill/decode disaggregation; KV cache offloading to CPU memory or storage; prompt/prefix caching across requests; routing and load balancing for LLMs; autoscaling and cold starts (model load times from storage); multi-model and LoRA serving; cost per token levers.

lessons.title: Vector databases in production: durability, scaling and operations
lessons.summary: Running vector search like any other critical datastore: replication, sharding, backups and upgrades.
lessons.covers: Index build vs query paths; sharding and replication strategies; write-ahead logs and durability; consistency of freshly inserted vectors; backup/restore and snapshotting of indexes; reindexing and embedding-model migrations without downtime; memory vs disk-based indexes and cost.
